messages:
sara: Heads up — since the CUDA driver bump last night we're seeing p99 spikes for short sequences (<32) on h100 pools. Noticed it after the 03:10 deploy.
jon: saw that too. p50 stable, but p99 up ~2.2x on small batches. Anything in autotuner logs?
kai: autotuner shows a different kernel path chosen for small seqs. It flipped from 'vectorized-attn' -> 'fallback-block' after driver 545.x. Hitrate for the preferred kernel dropped from 98% to ~48%.
lucy: confirmed on canary. KV-cache prefetch is also higher on the same requests, which seems correlated. More KV reads and longer memcopy time.
sara: timeline: driver upgrade at 02:50, small-seq p99 jump at ~03:05, increased KV prefetch latency at 03:07.
dmitri: attaching quick traces: ```
# perf summary
model: redwood-7b
seq=16 batch=8
kernel chosen: fallback-block
kv_prefetch: true
p99=210ms (was 92ms)
cpu memcpy 30ms
```
jon: hmm. Looks like kernel selector scoring now penalizes vectorized path because the driver exposes slightly different occupancy numbers -> autotuner re-ranked kernels. Combined with KV prefetch the overall latency increased.
kai: believe root cause: small change in reported SM config after driver bump causes our heuristic to favor kernels with lower theoretical complexity but worse memcopy profile on our KV prefetch path.
lucy: can we short-circuit KV prefetch as a quick mitigation? Maybe a runtime circuit-breaker flag to disable prefetch for small seqs while we patch selector.
sara: +1. If we can toggle kv_prefetch=false at route-level, we can observe delta quickly. Who can push it?
dmitri: I can flip a config on the canary pool. My plan: set kv_prefetch=false for route /v1/generate on canary h100, monitor p99 and backend traces for 10 minutes.
jon: also add a temporary kernel score override: prefer vectorized-attn for seq<=32. That's safer than a full rollback and should restore latency while we fix autotuner.
dmitri: will do both. Pushing canary change now.
infra-bot: deploy started: route-config-update for canary h100 by dmitri.
dmitri: done. kv_prefetch=false + kernel-override applied. Waiting 2min for metrics funnel.
sara: results?
dmitri: early numbers: p99 down from 210ms -> 104ms. p50 unchanged. KV-prefetch ops dropped 87%. Looks promising.
lucy: sweet. Can we roll to 10% traffic next? Need to be careful — prefetch is beneficial for longer sequences.
jon: we should also prepare a proper autotuner patch: include driver/GLIBC/driver-reported SM attrs into kernel scoring, and add a microbenchmark pass during canary startup to verify kernel timings and lock-in good candidate. This avoids heuristic flips on minor driver telemetries.
kai: agreed. Suggested patch: when driver version changes, force a microbench for seq=8/16/32 and record kernel latencies; use that data as a prior for the selector. Also add hysteresis so one upgrade doesn't flip thousand hosts.
sara: timeline: dmitri to expand canary to 10% if stable for 30m. kai/jon to draft autotuner PR with microbench + hysteresis. lucy to monitor long-seq regressions if we disable prefetch on more pools.
dmitri: opening canary -> 10% now. infra-bot: rollout started -> canary->10% by dmitri.
deploy-bot: smoke checks passed for route-config-update on canary.
jon: if autotuner PR takes longer, alternative is to scope kernel-override to driver-version tag: if driver >=545.x then use vectorized-attn for seq<=32. That buys time.
kai: ok I'll prototype selector change today. Will include tests: simulated driver attr changes with synthetic microbench and assert no flip without microbench failing.
lucy: one more: add a runtime metric: kernel-selector-change-rate (per host) and an alert if >3 flips/min. That will let ops catch noisy upgrades.
sara: good call. Also add a circuit-breaker endpoint so SRE can disable the selector heuristic entirely per pool in emergencies.
dmitri: I'll add the circuit-breaker flag to the pool config API (route-level), plus a one-click rollback that reverts route-config to previous commit.
jon: postmortem tasks: list root cause, the heuristic change, and the mitigation steps (kv_prefetch toggle, kernel override, microbench). Also coordinate with infra team to throttle driver rollout in future.
kai: PR coming. I'll try to keep changes minimal: prefer adding a microbench and prior weight instead of reworking whole selector.
sara: thanks everyone. Keep this thread updated with numbers. If anything worsens after canary->10% we pause rollout and rollback driver if needed. :thumbsup:
